Mr. Abdul Ali, learned counsel holding brief of Mr.
Bhupesh Kandpal, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. B.C. Joshi, learned AGA along with Mr. Vipul
Painuly, learned Brief Holder for the State.
3. By means of the present criminal writ petition,
petitioner has sought the following reliefs:-
"(a) A writ, order or direction in nature of mandamus
directing the respondent authorities to register the FIR
against the private respondent and further investigate in
accordance with law.
(b) A writ, order or direction in nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to decide the representation
dated 17.11.2024 in accordance with law (annexure-1 to
the writ petition)."
4. In substance by filing the instant writ petition,
petitioner wants this Court to direct the respondent
authorities to register the FIR against the private
respondent and to investigate it.
5. This kind of writ petition cannot be entertained.
Petitioner has got remedy for it under the law, in
particular, under Section 175(3) of BNSS [Old Section
156(3) Cr.P.C.] to approach the Magistrate of
competent jurisdiction to issue such a direction, but that
too can be availed only when the attempt for
registration of FIR by the SHO concerned, and,
thereafter, SSP has resulted into a futile exercise. From
the pleadings in the writ petition, there is nothing to

2
suggest that petitioner ever approached Police Station
concerned for lodging of an FIR.
6. In this view of the matter, the writ petition is quite
frivolous and deserves to be dismissed. Accordingly, the
same is dismissed.
7. Pending application, if any, stands disposed of
accordingly.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
